$comment: The lobby: what a guest can see in the weeks before the party. Presentation and costume only, never plot, which is why it is plaintext beside the encoded bible. A beat writes a character as {{C3}} and the name is substituted when it is served, so no character name is ever written down here.

copy.title: Before the night
copy.standfirst: You are cast. Here is who the room thinks you are, and what to wear. Everything private to you opens when the doors do.
copy.doorsNote: Your dossier, your secret and everything you are carrying into that room unlock at 7:00 on the night. Not before, not for anyone.

beats.title: The hall is booked. Actually booked.
beats.body: Third time asking. {{C1}} has the receipt, laminated, and has offered to show it to anyone who doubts it. The banner has been located. It has been in a box since 1991 and it smells like a box that has been closed since 1991. It is going up anyway.

beats.title: On the subject of the music
beats.body: There has been a disagreement about the playlist. One faction wants the year only. The other faction has pointed out that we graduated in June and the good songs came out in the autumn. A compromise has not been reached. Bring requests; bring stamina.

beats.title: Somebody found the yearbooks
beats.body: Two of them, plus the one with the page torn out that everybody remembers and nobody will admit to. They are coming. So is a slide projector that may or may not work. If you have photographs, bring photographs. People are going to want to look at each other at seventeen before they look at each other now.

beats.title: Tomorrow
beats.body: Doors at seven, and it starts at seven, so seven-thirty means walking in during your own introduction. Charge your phone; it is the only thing you have to bring and it holds everything that is yours. Wear the year. Eat something first, then eat again when you get here.

C1.attire: Committee-chair energy: a bright top or polo in school colors, pleated khakis or a denim skirt, white sneakers, and a name tag worn proudly all night. Going further, add a hand-lettered sash or a button reading CLASS OF '89, a fanny pack full of spare pens, and hair with as much volume as you can talk it into. Anything that looks like it was planned weeks in advance is exactly right.

C2.attire: Smart-casual grown-up: a blazer over a plain tee, dark jeans or trousers, and good shoes. Going further, put shoulder pads under the blazer, add a chunky watch, and carry a leather portfolio or a brick-sized phone around all night. The look is the classmate who dressed one notch above everybody else and knows it.

C3.attire: The teacher everybody loved: a corduroy or tweed jacket with elbow patches, a turtleneck or blouse, sensible shoes, and reading glasses on a chain. Going further, add a brooch, a scarf knotted with real commitment, and a worn paperback in the pocket. Comfort is correct here, since this is somebody who has been on their feet at events like this for decades.

C4.attire: Off duty but never quite off: a plain button-down or polo tucked in, dark jeans, a belt, and boots. Going further, add a department-looking windbreaker or ball cap, a mustache real or otherwise, and aviator sunglasses hooked in the collar. Neat and pressed beats fancy for this one.

C5.attire: Photographer black: dark jeans or trousers, a black shirt or roll-neck, flat comfortable shoes, and a real camera on a strap if you can borrow one. Going further, add a canvas vest or jacket with too many pockets, keep a lens cap in hand all evening, and wear slim eighties wire-frame glasses. Practical, unfussy, and slightly apart from the party.

C6.attire: The jacket is the whole costume: a letterman or varsity jacket over a plain tee, jeans, and white high-tops. Going further, add a class ring, a whistle, and a school-color sweatband worn without a trace of irony. If there is no varsity jacket to be found, any sports jacket with a patch pinned on will read from across the room.

C7.attire: Hardware-store practical: a flannel or work shirt over a tee, jeans, and boots. Going further, add a canvas work jacket, a store-branded cap, and a multi-tool on the belt. This is one of the easiest outfits on the list and looks right in any decade, which is entirely the point.

C8.attire: Neat and slightly over-prepared: a sweater vest or cardigan over a collared shirt, pressed trousers, and loafers. Going further, add a skinny tie, wire-rim glasses, a calculator watch, and a pocket organizer. Tuck everything in, because the tidiness is the joke.

C9.attire: Dressed to host: a nice shirt or blouse with the sleeves pushed up, dark trousers, and shoes you can stand in for four hours. Going further, wear an eighties statement blazer with the sleeves rolled, plenty of gold jewelry, and hair that clearly took effort. Being slightly too dressed up for a school hall is perfect here.

C10.attire: Came straight from work: a collared shirt and trousers or a simple dress, comfortable shoes, and a pager or phone that keeps going off. Going further, keep a stethoscope in a bag rather than around the neck, add an eighties-wide tie or a shoulder-padded jacket, and push reading glasses up into the hair. Tidy, tired, and a bit rumpled by nine o'clock.

F1.attire: Loud and comfortable: a bright windbreaker or tank over a tee, track pants or jeans, and sneakers. Going further, add a headband, a gym bag, an eighties windbreaker in colors that should not be together, and a shaker bottle carried all night. Sunglasses worn indoors are entirely in character.

F2.attire: Guest-of-a-guest smart: whatever you would wear to a nice party, plus one deliberate eighties touch such as big earrings, a bold belt, or a patterned blouse. Going further, commit to full shoulder pads in a statement color, since this is somebody who dressed up for a party they had no obligation to enjoy. Nothing here has to look strictly period.

F3.attire: Slightly too cool for the room: a denim or leather jacket over a band tee, jeans, and boots. Going further, add sunglasses, a bandana, a few rings, and hair that has not been rethought since the late eighties. The look should suggest somebody who never checked whether there was a dress code.

F4.attire: Working the event: black trousers or jeans, a black or white shirt, an apron or bar towel over the shoulder, and flat shoes. Going further, clip on a tie, roll the sleeves, and keep a bottle opener and a stack of napkins on you all evening. This is the one person in the room who does not have to dress period at all.

F5.attire: Respectable and a bit formal: a blazer or cardigan, a blouse or button-down, neat trousers or a knee-length skirt, and low heels or flats. Going further, try a pussy-bow blouse, pearls, and hair that has been set rather than styled. Aim for somebody dressed to be taken seriously by people much younger than them.

F6.attire: Roadie practical: a black tee, jeans, sneakers, and a lanyard or laminate around the neck. Going further, add a tool pouch or a roll of tape on the belt, a headset, and a checked shirt tied around the waist. Pockets matter more than period accuracy here, which is true to the character anyway.

F7.attire: Diner-shift comfortable: a simple shirt or blouse, jeans or a plain skirt, an apron, and shoes made for standing. Going further, add a name-tag pin, a pencil behind the ear, an order pad in the apron pocket, and a coffee pot to carry around. Genuinely the easiest outfit on this list.

F8.attire: Shop teacher forever: a plaid or work shirt, a zip cardigan or work jacket, comfortable trousers, and sturdy shoes. Going further, add a shop apron, a pencil behind the ear, glasses on a cord, and a cap that has clearly been owned for decades. Comfort first, since this character is happiest sitting down and holding court.

F9.attire: Easy and unbothered: a soft sweater or polo, neat jeans or chinos, and comfortable shoes. Going further, try a pastel eighties sweater with a collar popped underneath and hair with a bit of period volume. The point is somebody who dressed for a pleasant evening rather than for an audience.

F10.attire: Working press: a rumpled button-down, a loosened tie, a jacket, and comfortable shoes. Going further, keep a notebook and pen out all night and add a camera or a small recorder and a press card in a pocket. Deliberately not period, since this one graduated well after 1989.
